questions.title: Match Versus Search
questions.description: Which statement about re.match and re.search is TRUE?
questions.subtopic: Pattern Matching with search and match
questions.Option1: re.match only succeeds when the pattern matches at the very beginning of the string, while re.search finds the pattern anywhere in it
questions.Option2: re.search only succeeds at the beginning of the string
questions.Option3: re.match scans the whole string exactly like re.search
questions.Option4: Both require the pattern to match the entire string

questions.title: Digit Shorthand Meaning
questions.description: In a Python regular expression, what does \d match?
questions.Option1: Any single digit from 0 to 9
questions.Option2: Any letter or digit
questions.Option3: The literal letter d

questions.title: Word Character Shorthand
questions.description: Which characters does the shorthand class \w match?
questions.Option1: Letters, digits and the underscore
questions.Option2: Only lowercase and uppercase letters
questions.Option3: Letters, digits and whitespace

questions.title: Character Class Alternation
questions.Option1: Exactly one character that is a, b or c
questions.Option2: The whole three-letter string abc
questions.Option3: A sequence ab followed by c
questions.Option4: Any character except a, b or c

questions.title: Function Returning All Matches
questions.description: Which re function returns ALL non-overlapping matches of a pattern in a string as a list?
questions.Option1: re.findall
questions.Option2: re.search
questions.Option3: re.match

questions.title: Substitute All Digits
questions.Option1: a#b#
questions.Option2: a1b2
questions.Option3: ab

questions.title: Plus Quantifier
questions.description: In regex, what does the + quantifier mean?
questions.Option1: One or more repetitions of the preceding item
questions.Option2: Zero or more repetitions of the preceding item
questions.Option3: Exactly one repetition of the preceding item
questions.Option4: Zero or one repetition of the preceding item

questions.title: Star Quantifier
questions.description: In regex, what does the * quantifier mean?
questions.Option1: Zero or more repetitions of the preceding item
questions.Option2: One or more repetitions of the preceding item
questions.Option3: Exactly two repetitions of the preceding item
questions.Option4: One optional repetition of the preceding item

questions.title: Dot Meaning
questions.description: By default, what does the . metacharacter match in a Python regex?
questions.Option1: Any single character except a newline
questions.Option2: Any single character including the newline
questions.Option3: Only the literal dot character

questions.title: Raw String Benefit
questions.description: Why do Python programmers usually write regex patterns as raw strings like r"\d+"?
questions.Option1: Backslashes stay literal, so \d reaches the regex engine instead of being processed by Python first
questions.Option2: Raw strings make the pattern case-insensitive
questions.Option3: Raw strings make matching measurably faster
questions.Option4: re functions refuse pattern strings that are not raw

questions.title: Findall Group Tuples
questions.Option1: [('a', '1'), ('b', '22'), ('c', '3')] — when the pattern has two groups, findall returns tuples of the group values
questions.Option2: ['a=1', 'b=22', 'c=3'] — findall returns the full matches
questions.Option3: ['a', '1', 'b', '22', 'c', '3'] — groups come back flattened into one list
questions.Option4: [('a=1',), ('b=22',), ('c=3',)] — each match is a one-element tuple

questions.codesnippet:
import re
s = "<a><b>"
print(re.findall(r"<.*>", s))
print(re.findall(r"<.*?>", s))
questions.title: Greedy Versus Lazy
questions.Option1: ['<a><b>'] on the first line and ['<a>', '<b>'] on the second — greedy * takes everything up to the last >, lazy *? stops at the first
questions.Option2: ['<a>', '<b>'] on the first line and ['<a><b>'] on the second
questions.Option3: Both lines print ['<a>', '<b>']

questions.codesnippet:
import re
s = "error 404 at line 9"
print(re.match(r"\d+", s))
print(re.search(r"\d+", s).group())
questions.title: Anchored Match Failure
questions.subtopic: Pattern Matching with search and match
questions.Option1: None on the first line and 404 on the second — match anchors at the start where no digit sits, search finds the first run anywhere
questions.Option2: 404 on the first line and 404 on the second
questions.Option3: None on the first line and None on the second
questions.Option4: 404 on the first line and 9 on the second

questions.title: Backreference Swap
questions.Option1: 3456-12 - the replacement \2-\1 emits group 2 first, then group 1
questions.Option2: 12-3456 — re.sub ignores backreferences in the replacement
questions.Option3: 3456-12-12-3456 — both groups are emitted twice

questions.title: Quantifier Range Meaning
questions.description: What does the quantifier {2,4} mean in a regex?
questions.Option1: Repeat the preceding item at least 2 and at most 4 times, taking as many as possible
questions.Option2: Repeat the preceding item exactly 2 times or exactly 4 times
questions.Option3: Repeat the preceding item at least 4 times and at most 2 more
questions.Option4: Match the 2nd through 4th occurrence in the string

questions.codesnippet:
import re
print(re.findall(r"cat", "Cat CAT cat", re.I))
questions.title: Case Insensitive Flag
questions.Option1: ['Cat', 'CAT', 'cat'] — the re.I flag makes the match case-insensitive
questions.Option2: ['cat'] — only the lowercase occurrence matches
questions.Option3: ['Cat'] — only the first occurrence matches
questions.Option4: [] — the pattern cannot match mixed-case text

questions.codesnippet:
import re
s = "cat catalog concat cat"
print(len(re.findall(r"\bcat\b", s)))
questions.title: Word Boundary Count
questions.Option1: 2 - \b requires word boundaries, so catalog and concat do not count
questions.Option2: 4 — every cat substring counts
questions.Option3: 1 — only the last standalone cat counts

questions.codesnippet:
import re
m = re.search(r"((\d+)-(\d+))", "id 12-345")
print(m.group(1))
print(m.group(3))
questions.title: Nested Group Numbering
questions.Option1: 12-345 on the first line and 345 on the second — group 1 is the outer pair, group 3 is the last inner group
questions.Option2: 12-345 on the first line and 12 on the second
questions.Option3: 12 on the first line and 345 on the second
questions.Option4: 345 on the first line and 12-345 on the second

questions.title: Bounded Quantifier Greed
questions.Option1: ['aaaa', 'aa'] — each match grabs up to 4 a's, then scanning resumes after it
questions.Option2: ['aaaaaa'] — one match spans the whole run
questions.Option3: ['aa', 'aa', 'aa'] — the range always stops at its minimum

questions.codesnippet:
import re
m = re.search(r"(?P<user>\w+)@(?P<host>\w+)", "mail bob@site")
print(m.group("user"), m.group("host"))
questions.title: Named Group Extraction
questions.Option1: bob site — named groups (?P<name>...) can be fetched by label via .group('name')
questions.Option2: mail site — the host group eats the rest of the string
questions.Option3: user host — the group names themselves are printed
questions.Option4: bob@site site — the user group includes the @
